# Independent audit: section descent, strict contact, and the parity count

Audited source:
`candidate 4c405e76fb81c248`.

Dependencies independently re-read in their full stated scope:

- `historical context (not an accepted premise)`;
- `candidate 04819028a2421217`;
- the support-face and proper-section derivative proofs in
  `candidate 568f7cf028ec23b6`.

Conclusion: PASS. The source proves a structural deepest-point count,
not the OC depth fraction. The only wording qualification requested is
listed in Section 6 below.

## 1. Proper-section descent and strict contact

Let the actual attaining cap through Y have normal N=(a,u), u nonzero.
For a finite family of positive d-volume fibers, a proper cut contributes
its signed section integral divided by ||u|| to a normal perturbation.
A strict full or empty cut contributes zero. A supporting cut with
H_(d-1)-null trace contributes zero from both sides, by the separately
proved support-face formula. Hence the stated hypotheses do give a
linear two-sided derivative in every ambient normal direction.

Writing the differentiating section measure as nu, cap minimality under
all normal perturbations through Y gives

    integral (X-Y) dnu(X)=0.

Its positive mass W therefore makes its centroid exactly Y. This
statement uses the full ambient section point X, including its integer
base. It is not merely a fiberwise or continuous-coordinate balance.

For a distinct Y' in the original boundary plane, let Delta=Y'-Y. The
perturbed normal N+epsilon Delta with boundary through Y' defines the
same original cap when epsilon=0, because N.Delta=0. The continuous
normal remains nonzero for sufficiently small epsilon. Its derivative is

    (1/||u||) integral Delta.(X-Y') dnu(X)
      =-(W/||u||)||Delta||^2<0.

Thus an actual cap through Y' has smaller mass for all sufficiently small
positive epsilon. This gives strict inequality at every different point
of the plane, not just at other section centers. The Euclidean inner
product and coarea factor are used in the same original coordinates;
no nonisometric shear is being treated as an isometry.

A point in the strict interior of the original cap also has depth below
Q: move its original boundary a small positive distance into that cap,
less than the point's positive margin. At least one proper positive-
volume fiber supplies a slab of strictly positive volume, so the mass
strictly decreases. Thus the actual cap meets the ambient superlevel
set {D>=Q} at its source alone. W>0 is essential for this argument and
has not been dropped from the local lemma.

## 2. Finite-tilt attainment truly has arbitrary finite-base scope

The dependency works with every finite P subset R^n, without spacing,
rank, or convex-position hypotheses. Along a minimizing sequence, pass
to extended limits of each scalar a_k.(z-j). The finite-limit vectors
span a subspace L; subtract the convergent restriction P_L a_k and
replace it by its limit. This fixes the finite scalars exactly while
preserving the signs of all divergent scalars. One sufficiently large
finite index then saturates every divergent fiber. Thus a finite tilt
realizes the exact limiting mass, with the limiting unit continuous
normal, not merely an arbitrarily close mass.

Dominated convergence holds in each full-dimensional continuous fiber,
because every plane with unit continuous normal has zero d-volume.
The same construction proves lower semicontinuity of the optimized cap
function; a fixed attained tilt proves upper semicontinuity. The explicit
uniform slab bound proves Lipschitz continuity in the source's continuous
coordinates. Compactness of the unit continuous sphere supplies a
nonvertical attaining normal. Vertical containing caps can be replaced
by finite large tilts that capture no more mass, including the fibers
on their integer-boundary plane. Thus they do not create an unexamined
attainment failure.

These arguments are valid for d>=1 and arbitrary fixed real source base.
The additional interior-anchor hypothesis in the dependency's later
active-normal balance is not needed for its attainment and continuity
claims. The source uses the correct earlier portion of that theorem.

## 3. Boundary exclusion supplies positive section mass at maxima

The independently audited intrinsic bound gives

    D_S(z,y)<=N f_(C_z)(y)

on every maximal-dimensional positive-measure fiber, and depth zero on
all lower-dimensional fibers. Its proof establishes the necessary
parallelism of direction spaces only within each returning barycentric
combination before invoking intrinsic Brunn--Minkowski. It does not
assume parallelism for all fibers. Its finite affine-majorant step and
source-only limiting step do not require bounded selected tilts.

For q=d the ordinary own-fiber depth vanishes on the fiber boundary.
Consequently every positive-depth point is in the interior of a positive
full-dimensional fiber. At least one such point has positive depth: the
centroid of any positive fiber contributes a positive ordinary centroid
lower bound to every containing cap. Finite-fiber continuity and compact
positive fibers give an attained positive global maximum; omitted
lower-dimensional fibers all have depth zero.

Every nonvertical cap through such a maximum has a proper own-fiber cut.
Its H_(d-1) section measure is positive. This proves the W>0 condition
used by strict contact at the actual maximizers. It does not improperly
infer this condition for arbitrary supporting or saturated source caps.

## 4. Parity and strictly convex fibers

Depth superlevels in the full ambient space are convex: a closed
halfspace containing a segment point contains at least one endpoint, so
its mass is at least the smaller endpoint depth. If two distinct actual
global deepest points have equal integer parity, their midpoint is in
C by convexity and has an integer base. It is therefore an actual mixed
point and, by this quasiconcavity, another global deepest point.

Choose the qualifying actual critical cap at this midpoint. It contains
at least one endpoint. Strict contact proves that endpoint has depth
strictly smaller than the common maximum, a contradiction. There is
thus at most one deepest point per parity class. An explicitly chosen
basis of the full affine base lattice gives the stronger bound 2^r
when the measured base set has affine rank r.

For d>=2 a supporting face of a strictly convex positive fiber is a
singleton, hence H_(d-1)-null. Every actual nonvertical minimizing cap
therefore satisfies the required derivative regularity, and its proper
own section supplies positive mass. This proves the unconditional
structural corollary for strictly convex positive fibers: at most 2^n
actual global deepest points. The exclusion of d=1 here is correct,
since H_0 of a singleton is one, not zero. Varying intrinsic fiber planes
are also correctly left outside this corollary.

For C=[0,1]^n times a centered Euclidean d-ball, every cube-vertex base
can be isolated by a finite large integer tilt, simultaneously excluding
all other bounded fibers while retaining a prescribed continuous cap on
the chosen fiber. Its mixed depth is therefore exactly its own ordinary
ball depth. Own-fiber contributions give the opposite inequality. The
ordinary ball depth reaches half its volume only at its center; each
nonzero source has an outward radial cap of strictly smaller volume.
Thus exactly the 2^n fiber centers are deepest. This verifies sharpness
of the COUNT, not sharpness of a claimed OC bound.

## 5. Roof family and transverse interval

The roof model is a convex body: its lower roof is constant and its
upper roof g is positive, continuous, and concave. The reflected subset
with lower roof -g(-z,-s) is actually contained in the body, is centrally
symmetric about the source, and has exactly twice the positive cap mass.
Reflection preserves both the integer lattice and the mixed measure.
Every closed containing halfspace contains at least half that subset's
mass, even if a vertical boundary carries mixed mass. The positive cap
attains the lower bound. This proves full-normal source depth, not just
stationarity or integer-tilt optimality.

For the transverse family, the lower condition on h puts
2h-g(-z,-s) above -L throughout D. The paired-roof condition makes every
interval nonempty, and h<=min g makes the claimed through-source cap
mass exactly Q-hW. Reflection about the actual source (0,0,h) preserves
the mixed lattice and gives the matching lower bound. The source belongs
to its actual fiber. In the explicit rational model the entire interval
[-3/8,1/4] and the exact depth 15/2-6h follow as stated.

The source at height zero is not declared globally deepest; the lower
symmetric cylinder gives an actual deeper source when L is large. The
example therefore correctly refutes transfer from a deep derivative
section while preserving the distinction from global source optimality.
The two-sided Fubini decomposition retains both overhang terms and does
not silently identify section length with either cap's volume.

Ran `work/math-venv/bin/python supporting computation verify_proper_section_roof_transverse_certificate.py`:

    97 exact rational checks passed.

## 6. Minor wording precision

In Section 1, the assertion that every restricted ambient halfspace is
a halfspace in the reduced affine coordinates should explicitly allow
the whole reduced affine space or the empty set when the normal vanishes
on that affine space. A trace containing the actual source cannot be
empty; a whole-space trace captures all mass and is harmless to a depth
infimum. The converse extension of every genuine reduced halfspace is
valid. This qualification does not affect any argument above.

## 7. Provenance: the parity count is an alternative derivation

The stricter interpolation argument in
`candidate f2d1fbdd5a877f5b`, Section 3,
already establishes the null-facet/strict-convex parity corollary. The
new section-centroid proof gives a valid alternative derivation and the
explicit derivative certificate; it must not be presented as discovery
of a previously unproved cardinality theorem. This provenance correction
does not change the mathematical PASS above.

## 8. Independent audit of the new arbitrary-centered-section roof lemma

The new Sections 11--12 also PASS. Full affine span of the mixed support
and mean zero imply a positive positive-part moment in every unit
direction: if it were zero, the negative moment must also vanish and
the support would lie in that direction's zero plane. Bounded support
makes the moment continuous, giving m0>0 on the compact unit sphere.
The radius R is taken on the measured support, which is sufficient for
all integrals, and is positive. No symmetry is used.

For positive vertical-normal coefficient, the fiber-by-fiber cap mass
minus Q is exactly integral clip(ell,-g,L). Replacing -g by -G gives a
lower bound. When kR<=L the positive linear moment is untruncated and
mean zero bounds the negative term. When kR>L, the elementary bound
min(kx,L)>=(L/R)x on [0,R] gives positive term at least LWm0/R>=GW,
while the negative term is at most GW. These arguments include every
linear functional on the full section coordinates, not merely its
continuous directions.

For negative vertical coefficient, the cap contains the full lower
segment over the section halfspace ell>=0. Its measure is bounded
below by L times that halfspace's mass, and the positive-part moment
bound gives at least LWm0/R>=GW>=Q. The zero functional is handled
separately. Zero vertical coefficient obeys the same section-mass
bound. Pure integer directions and their possible boundary mass only
increase it. A general containing cap contains its parallel through-
source cap. Thus the proof gives actual full-normal minimizing depth,
not just stationarity. The source is an actual mixed point and all
positive original fibers have proper flat cuts.

In the rational example, the mixed support radius is 19/10. Pairing the
outer intervals contributes at least 2|a| to the absolute moment; the
central symmetric subinterval contributes 121|b|/100 independently.
After dividing by 2W=10, the unit-direction lower bound 121/1000 is
valid, and 50 m0/R>=121/38>31/10. Recomputed Q=10 and M=260. The
contained middle rectangle of area 150 gives an actual different
source raw depth at least 75, correctly excluding any global-maximizer
interpretation of the roof's source.

The section-center proof includes upward, downward, and pure integer
halfspaces and proves unique global center Z=(0,1), depth two. The
strictly better section source lifts to a point with the explicit
original cap t>=(x-1)/40. Its threshold is proper throughout every
fiber, and its exact area is 10-(1/40)(11/2-5)=799/80<10. The positive-
roof transfer fraction is 11/50<2/9, whereas the section and negative-
side fractions are 2/5. Every inequality and source membership checks.

Re-ran `work/math-venv/bin/python supporting computation verify_proper_section_roof_transverse_certificate.py`:

    97 exact rational checks passed.
    111 total exact rational checks passed after nonsymmetric extension.

## 9. Strict-no-heavy supplement, Section 13

section length 7/2. The paired outer intervals and the actual central
symmetric subinterval give m0>=289/5488; R<=2 suffices, and
40m0/R>=1445/1372>1. Thus the general all-normal realization lemma
applies. The three original areas 41,123/2,41 are all strictly below
287/4. The piecewise clipped outer tails establish the section's unique
center x=5/8 at raw depth 13/8 in both continuous orientations, and
pure integer caps are larger. The explicit original cap t>=5/8-x is
proper on every fiber and has area 55/16<7/2. Finally the actual central
reflection intersection has section lengths 3/4,5/4,3/4 and height41,
so its half-mass451/8 exceeds the OC target287/9. The example therefore
has the asserted strict no-heavy property and section-lifting failure,
while expressly satisfying OC and having a different deeper original
source. Re-ran the verifier: all123 exact rational checks passed.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
